# WIAI Datastore

> End-to-end encrypted key-value storage for single-file web apps (one HTML file, opened from file://, a local web server or Electron), run by the Faculty of Information Systems and Applied Computer Sciences (WIAI), University of Bamberg. The server stores only ciphertext, with one exception by design: the faculty holds a recovery (escrow) key.

You are probably the Claude of a developer who wants an app to keep its data here, a new app or an existing one. Read {{base}}/docs/integration.md first: the script tag with its integrity hash, the Content-Security-Policy, the API and a complete example. An existing app: also read {{base}}/docs/porting.md first. Current library: version {{version}}, {{library_url}}. Source, PROTOCOL.md and the verifier wds-verify: {{repo_url}}

## The rules that matter

1. Load the library with exactly one script tag from integration.md and put its Content-Security-Policy meta tag before every script; never copy, inline, modify or self-host the library, load no other third-party script, add no hosts to script-src or connect-src.
2. All user data goes through the object from WDS.connect(): no own cryptography, no fetch/XHR/WebSocket to the datastore, no user data in localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB or cookies (a preference chosen from a fixed list, such as theme or last tab, may stay in localStorage).
3. Never build passphrase, login or key dialogs and never ask for a passphrase or access ID: call store.unlock() and let the library's dialogs do it; they follow <html lang>.
4. One record per entity; many items or files go into store.collection(); editors use store.autosave(), never store.set() on every keystroke.
5. Give the app one "Vault" button that calls store.openVault() (members, access sheet, passphrase, export, lock) and hide edit controls for read members with the data-wds-role attribute on <html>.
6. Download only what the person clicks for, with a note that the file is not encrypted; never download in the background.
7. Data that an old version left in IndexedDB or localStorage is taken over with store.migrateLocal(), not with code of your own (porting.md).
8. Before hand-over run wds-verify from a clone of {{repo_url}} (integration.md, "wds-verify"), fix what it reports and put the report into the app's README.

## Pages

- {{base}}/docs/integration.md and {{base}}/docs/porting.md - the developer guides for you (HTML at the same address without .md)
- {{base}}/docs/users.en.md and {{base}}/docs/users.de.md - for the people who use the app; {{base}}/docs/operator.md - for the operator of the service
- {{base}}/export/ - standalone tool that unlocks a vault and downloads everything, decrypted, as a ZIP
- {{base}}/ - dashboard for faculty staff: register a scope, get the scope ID, the join code and one text for you, which is also the section for the app's CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md
- {{api_url}} - HTTP API of the library (app code never calls it; wire format: PROTOCOL.md in the repository)

## Facts to quote correctly

- Wherever you describe the privacy of an app, use this sentence word for word (a text in another language uses the English one):
  en: Data is end-to-end encrypted; the faculty holds a recovery key for emergencies.
  de: Die Daten sind Ende-zu-Ende-verschlüsselt; die Fakultät verwahrt für Notfälle einen Wiederherstellungsschlüssel.
- A scope is one registered app, with an ID like notenrechner-k7m2a9. Every user has their own vault inside it; the owner can share a vault with others (roles write and read).
- Users unlock with an access ID and their own passphrase (at least 12 characters), which the server cannot reset. The access sheet holds the emergency code for the faculty recovery.
- Default limits: 10 MB per record, 200 MB per vault including history, the last 10 versions of every record (a scope may set other values: wds-verify prints them). 1 MB = 1,048,576 bytes.
- The service is online only. When the connection fails, the library offers a backup download of the unsaved values.
